summary: Louise Roche specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She held a post at the University of Munich's Institut für Indologie und Tibetologie in 2023 and is attested as an Assistentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma (attested 1999) and also studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Lourens P. van den Bosch works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Utrecht University (~1974–1978) under Jan Gonda, and also studied under Th. P. van Baaren, Johannes Hendrik Hospers, Fred Leemhuis, and Adam Simon van der Woude.
Lozang Samten studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.

Lozang Trinlae studied at Northeastern University, Harvard, and Claremont School of Theology (PhD 2011–2017). He was CEO of Educational Visions and Methods (1993–2009) and InsightSupport.Org (2018), and a visiting lecturer at the University of Tartu (2019–2021).
Lubomír Ondračka specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Dušan Zbavitel and held posts at Charles University (attested 1994–1999 and 2018).

Lubor Hájek was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University (1945–1949) under Otakar Pertold and Vincenc Lesný, and served as Director of Oriental Collections at the National Gallery Prague from 1952 to 1986.
Luboš Bělka specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University (~1978–1983) and held a post there around 1993.
Luca Brigada Villa works in linguistics, Indology, and computational fields. He has held posts at the University of Bergamo and the University of Pavia.

Luca Maria Olivieri is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who completed his doctoral degree at the Free University of Berlin in 2011. He directed the Italian Institute for Africa and the East (attested 2019) and taught at Ca' Foscari University.
Luchun Wu works in Buddhist studies and sinology. A PhD researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026), Wu also held a post at Ghent University in 2025.

Lucia Catherine Graeme Grieve studied at Wellesley College, Oxford, and Columbia University (Ph.D. ~1895–1898). She taught at several female seminaries and colleges between 1883 and 1893, working in the field of Indology.

Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held lecturer and associate professor posts at SOAS University of London (attested 2003–2015) and is attested as a visiting member at Minobusan University in 2026.
Lucia Galli is a Tibetologist who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

Lucian Scherman studied at Breslau and Munich under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Ernst Kuhn. An Indologist and archaeologist, he served as a professor at the University of Munich (1892–1933) and director of the Museum Fünf Kontinente (1907–1933).

Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and sinology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci (~1934–1939). He taught at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946) and held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984).

Lucien Bernot studied at INALCO and EPHE. Specializing in Tibetology and sinology, he worked at the CNRS (1947–1964), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1961–1978), and held a professorship at the Collège de France (1979–1985).

Lucien Lévy-Bruhl was a philosopher and scholar of religion who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne. He held a post at the University of Paris (~1899–1927) and founded the Institut d'ethnologie.

Linguist Lucien Tesnière studied at the University of Paris, University of Leipzig, and under Antoine Meillet at ENLOV. He held academic posts at the University of Ljubljana (~1920–1924), University of Strasbourg (1924–1937), and University of Montpellier (1937).
